same_event.instructions: Do `published` and `new` report the same specific event (the same incident, decision or episode)?

criteria.true: the same incident, decision or episode, possibly with more details or different wording
criteria.false: different events, even if the topic, place, war or type of event match; a different strike, a different day, a statement by a different person

same_event._note: Три атомарні noul замість одного choice same/follow_up/unrelated, як радить TypeSafe: одне складне питання давало 78% і надто часто follow_up. Разом з вердиктом у коді (nyan/jev.py: relation_verdict) — 90–93% на відкладених половинах 160 прод-пар проти сліпої розмітки за правилами relation.txt; прод-LLM на тих самих — 85–87%. Англійською, бо кирилиця в критеріях у 4–5 разів дорожча, а на точність мова критеріїв не впливала.

caused_by.instructions: Did the event in `new` happen as a direct consequence of the event in `published`?

criteria.true: without the published event this one would not have happened: arrest after a shooting, verdict after an arrest, signing after a vote, a reaction that names the published event
criteria.false: only a shared topic, country, process or war; the next attack; an independent statement

caused_by._note: Слабке місце: 8 з 37 продовжень Jev вважав не пов'язаними — такий пост вийде окремо, а не реплаєм.

facts_changed.instructions: Compared with `published`, does `new` materially change the facts of the same event?

criteria.true: death or injury toll changed, officially confirmed or denied, decision reversed
criteria.false: no material change, or it is a different event
